title: release-snapshot-timeline-and-signal-play-notes-2026-04-19
body:
Purpose and scope:
This working note captures a compact preflight timeline, a minimal checklist for the staging -> canary -> prod progression, and a focused set of observability 'signal plays' (what to watch, thresholds, and immediate actions). Intended audience: release conductor, on-call SRE, owning feature engineers, and the release engineer responsible for cutover.

Context:
- Release: sprint-2026-04-feature-snapshot (bundle of smaller infra and serving changes: batching tuning, KV cache tweak, two kernel swaps)
- Target prod cutover window: 2026-04-22 02:00-04:00 UTC (low-traffic window)
- Canary region: us-west-2 first, then eu-west-1 staggered + 30m

Compact rollout timeline (high level):
- D-3 (2026-04-19): Final smoke snapshot created; coordinator signoff call (15m).
- D-2 (2026-04-20): Staging sanity run (30m), perf histogram snapshot, rollout notes updated.
- D-1 (2026-04-21): Dry-run in staging with traffic replay; create canary manifests and TTL gates.
- D (2026-04-22): Canary->observe 60m in us-west-2; if green, expand 10% every 20m until 100%. If any circuit-breaker tripped, rollback to previous model variant and notify.
- D+1 (2026-04-23): Postmortem takeaways and telemetry patch if needed.

Preflight checklist (quick yes/no items - owner in parentheses):
- Is the release branch built and artifacts available in registry (CI job id)? (Ava)
- Smoke tests green on staging build (link to run) (Diego)
- Telemetry dashboards created/updated: per-route latency, P99 token latency, error-rate, QPS, GPU memory pressure (Priya)
- Canary manifests and consistent routing policy prepared (manifest sha) (Release engineer)
- Rollback artifact verified and easily redeployable (artifact id) (Platform)
- Pager duty rotation confirmed for release window (SRE lead)
- Runbook and quick rollback steps pinned to Slack channel #release-ops (Ava)
- Client SDK compatibility check (minor semver bump) (Devex)

Signal plays (observability -> escalation -> immediate action):
1) Token-level latency spike (user-facing)
- Signal: sustained P99 token latency > 350ms for 5m on production route(s) handling inference.
- Why: Indicates kernel mismatch or batching regression.
- Immediate action: Throttle new requests at the ingress (reduce concurrency), switch to compatible model variant (fallback model tag) if available, and open a tracing session for affected requests. Notify #release-ops with tag @oncall-sre.
- Escalation (15m): Rollback canary expansion and revert to prior runtime config.

2) Error rate increase (5xx)
- Signal: 5xx rate > 0.5% of traffic sustained for 3m or an absolute spike of >100 errors/min.
- Why: Could be resource exhaustion, mem leaks, or malformed inputs post-change.
- Immediate action: Pause canary expansion, route new traffic to previous capacity pool, run healthcheck script on canary nodes, collect core logs (last 5 minutes). If a single exception class dominates, attempt hotfix if low-risk.

3) GPU memory pressure / OOM warnings
- Signal: driver/kernel OOM logs appear or free GPU memory < 250MB for >2m per instance.
- Why: New kernel selection or quantization path may increase memory usage at certain sequence lengths.
- Immediate action: Reduce max-seq or bump instance type for canary only; if persists, rollback model variant.

4) Telemetry divergence (model quality)
- Signal: regression on synthetic prompt set > 3% for measured quality metric (BLEU-like or task-specific) within canary window.
- Why: New kernel/quantization causing output regressions.
- Immediate action: Stop expansion, trigger evaluation suite for full prompt set, escalate to applied-ml for triage.

Circuit-breaker matrix (short):
- Any single signal: pause expansion and investigate (do not auto-rollback unless actioned).
- Any two signals simultaneously or a hard threshold (e.g., 5xx > 2%) -> immediate rollback to previous canary and page SRE.

Canary expansion plan (timed steps):
- Step 0: Deploy canary (1% traffic) -> observe 15m for infra signals, 45m for quality signals.
- Step 1: Expand to 5% -> observe 20m.
- Step 2: Expand to 20% -> observe 20m.
- Step 3: Expand to 50% -> observe 30m.
- Step 4: Expand to 100% -> observe 60m then mark done.
Notes: If any pause during expansion, allow a minimum of 20m stable window before resuming.

Release notes draft (to be refined for public-facing summary):
Draft title: "Runtime and batching improvements — April snapshot"
Short summary: "This release deploys optimizations to the inference runtime that reduce per-token CPU/GPU overhead and improve small-sequence latency under typical production load. Includes KV cache handling fixes and two new kernel code-paths that reduce memory use for medium-context workloads."
Impact bullets (internal):
- Expected 5–12% cost-per-token reduction for chat-style traffic.
- Improved P95 token latency for short sequences (<=64 tokens).
- No API surface changes; client SDK remains compatible.
Known limitations and cautions:
- Some edge sequences may increase peak memory slightly — we pin circuit-breakers and have a fast rollback path.
- On-prem customers with custom kernel bundles should test before scheduling the upgrade; contact release-private@redwood.ai.

Post-release tasks (D+1 to D+7):
- Collect a focused telemetry pack (latency histograms, sample traces, error-class digest) (Diego)
- Finalize public release notes and send to comms (Ava)
- Retro: 30m postmortem with SRE, applied-ml and platform (Priya to schedule)
- If any regressions, create ticket with priority=P0/P1 and link to rollback artifacts

Quick links and artifacts to attach before D: (placeholders)
- Staging smoke run: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/8821
- Canary manifest SHA: sha256:abc123def456
- Regression test results (staging): https://ci.redwood.ai/tests/feature-snapshot/summary

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Should we widen the initial canary region to include eu-west-1 at 1% simultaneously? Pro: catches region-specific infra issues earlier. Con: increases blast radius. (Need SRE signoff)
- Do we enable the new batching heuristic by default for dedicated customers? Current plan: opt-in for Dedicated in the next maintenance window.
- Final owner for client SDK compatibility notes — who owns release announcement copy for DevEx?

Appendix: quick rollback commands (for release engineer)
- kubectl -n inference set image deployment/inference-service inference=registry.redwood.ai/inference:v2026-04-12-rollback
- platform deploy rollback --artifact sha256:abc123def456
- Route traffic: routingctl set-weight --service inference --subset previous 100

End of working note.

Action items (assign now):
- [Ava] pin final smoke run link and confirm CI artifact id.
- [Diego] update telemetry dashboard with P99 token-splits and enable alert suppression during expected cold-starts.
- [Priya] prepare applied-ml on-call for evaluation on D window.

Notes about doc quality: this is intentionally terse. Expand into a public release note and a separate step-by-step operator runbook if we intend to reuse this flow across teams.
